results.content:
Most marketing people are using AI wrong.

They type “write me a caption for Instagram” and then complain that the output sounds robotic. They paste a blog post and ask for “a summary” and get something flatter than a press release.

The problem isn’t Claude. The problem is that they’re using a Formula 1 car to go grocery shopping.

Claude.ai is not a content vending machine. It’s a strategic thinking partner — one that has read more case studies, ad copy teardowns, brand positioning documents, and consumer psychology papers than any single human ever could.

Once you treat it that way, everything changes.

I’m going to walk you through exactly how I use it — not for the easy stuff, but for the hard stuff that used to keep me up at night. [...] ## Part 1: Positioning and Messaging — Where Most Brands Get It Wrong

## The Prompt That Exposed Our Messaging Problem in 4 Minutes

I pasted our homepage copy into Claude and asked:

“Read this homepage copy. Tell me exactly what product/service this company sells, who it’s for, and what makes it different from competitors — using ONLY the words on this page. Then tell me what’s missing.”

The output was devastating.

Claude could identify our product. But it could not identify our customer. And it couldn’t articulate a single differentiator that wasn’t also on every competitor’s site.

We had written copy for ourselves. Not for our buyers.

That one prompt saved us from running a six-figure campaign on a broken foundation.

How do you know whether content was genuinely crafted by a human? And if you use AI responsibly in your workflow, how do you ensure your writing retains its natural, engaging rhythm instead of sounding cold and robotic? [...] ## 3. Write Threads and Posts That Actually Convert (The 4-Part Framework)

Claude is terrifyingly good at long-form threads because it thinks in narrative arcs.

Use this system:

1. Feed it a raw idea or insight from your business.
2. Tell it: “Turn this into a high-converting LinkedIn/X thread using my brand voice. Use the exact structure that gets maximum engagement: strong hook, personal story, 5-7 valuable insights, proof, and a clear call-to-action that feels natural, not salesy.”

The threads that come out feel like you stayed up until 2 a.m. writing from the soul — except you did it in 12 minutes.

## 4. The Repurposing Machine That Turns One Piece Into 30

This is where most entrepreneurs lose. They create once and move on.

The Claude system: [...] They know.

Prompt Claude like this:

“Act as a world-class market researcher. Analyze the last 50 comments/DMs/replies on my content [paste them]. What patterns are emerging? What unmet desires keep showing up? What specific language are people using when they’re most excited or frustrated? Give me 10 new content angles based on this.”

Do this every two weeks and your content becomes eerily on-point.

## 6. The Identity Shift That Makes All of This Sustainable

Here’s the layer almost nobody talks about:

The real power of using Claude isn’t the content output.

It’s who you become when you stop being the bottleneck in your own marketing.

Most entrepreneurs stay small on social because they believe “I have to do it myself to make it authentic.”
